items.title: Data centres in the U.S. put out more carbon emissions in a year than Denmark, says Harvard study
items.summary_auto: The 400 largest data centres in the United States put more heat-trapping gases into the atmosphere in one year than the entire nation of Denmark did, and that was before the artificial intelligence boom really got going, according to a Harvard University study published Monday.

items.title: Father calls for apology after son target of racist taunts at Kitchener, Ont., hockey tournament
items.summary_auto: The father of a 16-year-old hockey player says he wants a public apology and cultural-competency training for the league after his son was the target of racist taunts at a tournament in Kitchener, Ont., on Nov. 8.

items.title: The U.K. is granting pardons to women for past abortion convictions
items.summary_auto: The U.K. government says it will grant automatic pardons to all women convicted of having illegal abortions over the last 165 years.

items.title: Military's No. 2 defends GlobalEye surveillance jets despite capability concerns
items.summary_auto: Canada's second-in-command is standing behind the proposed purchase of six Saab GlobalEye surveillance jets despite air force concerns about their capabilities. Vice-Admiral Angus Topshee told MPs he's satisfied with the procurement process, arguing the aircraft will contribute to an integrated continental defence network alongside satellites and ground-based radar systems.

items.title: United Airlines says issue affecting departing flights has been resolved
items.summary_auto: United Airlines said Monday that it had resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, just days after a malfunction in the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration's network prompted a nationwide ground stop.

items.title: Journalists call for justice after reporter found dead in Mexican coastal city of Acapulco
items.summary_auto: A Mexican journalist was found dead on Saturday on the outskirts of Acapulco, a popular resort city in the southern Guerrero state, marking the latest in a string of alleged attacks targeting reporters in the country.

items.title: N.L. premier waiting to hear from Quebec on Churchill River power deal
items.summary_auto: Quebec Energy Minister Stéphane Paquet said the Churchill River power deal is not set in stone, setting off a series of questions for Premier Tony Wakeham in Newfoundland and Labrador's House of Assembly.

items.title: Gordie Howe bridge surpasses 1M vehicle crossings while other bridges, tunnel lose traffic
items.summary_auto: The Gordie Howe International Bridge has seen more than a million crossings since it officially opened to vehicle traffic on July 27, according to new numbers from the Bridge and Tunnel Operators Association.

items.title: Parents are skipping vitamin K shots for newborns
items.summary_auto: More parents are skipping vitamin K shots for newborns, but skipping it could lead to dangerous brain bleeds.

items.title: Alberta has tabled a bill for new riding maps. What could a court challenge mean?

items.title: Exodus in Poilievre's office as 5 staffers plan departures

items.summary_auto: French actor Gérard Depardieu has dropped his appeal of a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set, saying in a statement Monday that he would accept his 18-month suspended sentence.

items.title: Bank of Canada governor Tiff Macklem to step down in 2027
